correctness.rationale: Exact signed-tree decomposition of total inversions into gap signs times leaf-subtree size products. An independent-priority BST representation of the unsigned tree yields a two-sided truncated-geometric integral; integration by parts gives the harmonic weights. Bernoulli sign independence establishes full-vector conditional regression and peak covariances. Harmonic differences and strict concavity prove threshold ordering, while standard harmonic asymptotics prove the binary-entropy profile and boundary thresholds. Reconstructed hypotheses n>=2, 0<p<1, interior peaks only; exact rational Markov enumeration checks all signatures/covariances for 2<=n<=7 at p=1/2 and 2/3 (624 assertions). Finite checks do not prove asymptotics.

value.rationale: The question is how a global inversion statistic responds to the location of a local descent in a natural recursive nonuniform permutation model. The answer is a complete exact positional kernel with nontrivial binary-entropy bulk and logarithmic boundary behavior, and it yields an ordered family of genuinely different peak–inversion covariance transition probabilities (from 1/3 to 2/3 at the boundaries). This is a structural local/global dependence classification, not a textbook calculation of the binomial total-descent law, arbitrary parameter slice or finite-table recomputation.
